name: AES Corporation
reason: Levered global power generator/developer with net debt/EBITDA 8.2x, 10y avg ROIC 0.9%, negative 10y FCF conversion (-4.0x) and a 161% adjusted-vs-GAAP EPS gap; balance sheet and earnings quality fail the recession and forecastability tests.

name: Northeast Bank
reason: Niche national lender buying and originating discounted CRE/business loans with lumpy EPS (8.55 in 2021, -37.5% in 2022, now 12.74 at 1.0x 10y peak); 17% avg ROE is impressive but earnings hinge on loan-purchase discounts and credit outcomes that cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: Fulton Financial Corporation
reason: Ordinary mid-Atlantic regional bank with 10y avg ROE 9.5% and ROIC 6.7%, EPS at 1.0x 10y high after a rate tailwind and a 2020 drop of -22%; cheap (9.7x) but no specialness.

name: Universal Health Services, Inc.
reason: Hospital/behavioral operator with EPS at 1.0x 10y peak (21.74 vs 11.82 in 2021) boosted by Medicaid supplemental payments, a credible government-reimbursement threat within 5 years, and only 4/10 years of >=7% EPS growth.

name: Mattel, Inc.
reason: Hit- and retailer-driven toy maker with 10y EPS CAGR 1.1%, losses in 2017-2019, revenue CAGR -0.6% and 10y avg ROIC 2.1%; not forecastable and not special.

name: Blue Owl Capital Corporation
reason: BDC whose earnings are set by base rates and middle-market credit spreads (net debt/EBITDA 7.1x, consensus EPS -17.9% FY1 and negative LTG); a rate/credit-cycle lender with no route to 7% growth.

name: Affiliated Managers Group, Inc.
reason: Asset-management holding company whose fees track markets and fund flows (revenue CAGR -1.8% over 10y); EPS growth of 7.6% came from shrinking the share count 5.4%/yr, not the core business.

name: Sonic Automotive, Inc.
reason: Cyclical auto dealer with 3.6% EBIT margin, net debt/EBITDA 5.9x, acquisitions at 1.6x 10y FCF and a 91% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap; EPS still 0.69x the 2022 peak, so earnings follow the auto cycle.

name: Boston Scientific Corporation
reason: Share-gaining interventional medtech with secular drivers (Watchman LAAC, Farapulse PFA, an aging population): 10y revenue CAGR 10.5%, adj EPS CAGR 12.6% (26% over 5y) and 8/10 years >=7%, net debt/EBITDA 1.8x; caveats are heavy tuck-in M&A (acq 1.28x 10y FCF), a 134% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap and EBIT margin at its 10y high (100th pctile); the 13.4x NTM P/E in the data looks low against its usual multiple and should be checked.

name: MillerKnoll, Inc.
reason: Office-furniture maker in structural decline after the Knoll deal: EPS 0.56x its 10y max, 10y EPS CAGR -1.5%, net debt/EBITDA 4.5x for a cyclical, acquisitions at 1.05x FCF and a 121% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap.

name: Old Second Bancorp, Inc.
reason: Chicago-suburban community bank whose growth came from acquisitions (shares +5.3%/yr, acquisitions 0.61x 10y FCF) with EPS 0.8x its 2023 peak; ordinary franchise with no specialness.

name: KeyCorp
reason: Rate-sensitive super-regional bank with 10y EPS CAGR 3.6%, avg ROE 8.7%, shares +2.8%/yr and a -40.6% EPS hit in 2023 from securities/funding mismatch; underwriting and ALM record are not Buffett-grade.

name: Henry Schein, Inc.
reason: Low-margin dental/medical distributor (EBIT margin 5.9%, revenue CAGR 2.2%) with net debt/EBITDA 3.0x and acquisitions at 0.87x 10y FCF; EPS growth comes mainly from buybacks and deals, and online and private-label channels pressure the model.

name: Gen Digital Inc.
reason: Consumer cyber-safety roll-up (Norton/Avast/LifeLock/MoneyLion) with acquisitions at 1.91x 10y FCF, EBIT margin at a 10y high of 50% after cost-cutting, net debt/EBITDA 2.6x and a 58% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap; the risk of OS/AI disintermediation of standalone consumer security makes 10-year forecasting low-confidence.

name: Prudential Financial, Inc.
reason: Life insurer/asset manager whose earnings depend on rates, markets and mortality (10y EPS CAGR 3.7%, avg ROE 8.2%, -35% in 2022), with EPS at 0.99x its 10y peak and consensus LTG of 3.4%.

name: UGI Corporation
reason: Propane/LPG distributor plus utilities with net debt/EBITDA 4.45x, 10y avg ROIC 4.7%, shares +2.2%/yr, weather-driven earnings and secular volume decline at AmeriGas; EPS CAGR only 5.1%.

name: QCR Holdings, Inc.
reason: Impressively steady EPS compounding (14.4% 10y CAGR, 8/10 years >=7%, no down year) but shares +4.9%/yr from stock-funded bank acquisitions, a meaningful share of income from volatile LIHTC capital-markets fees, and concentrated LIHTC/CRE lending make durable forecasting uncertain.

name: Minerals Technologies Inc.
reason: Specialty-minerals business with 10y EPS CAGR 2.5% (2/10 years >=7%), 10y avg ROIC 5.4% and an unresolved talc-litigation overhang (BMI Oldco Chapter 11); no route to 7% growth.

name: Tompkins Financial Corporation
reason: Upstate-NY community bank with 10y avg ROE 11.4%; reported EPS swung from 0.66 (2023 securities loss) to 11.24 in 2025 on one-off gains, with consensus FY1 EPS -30.6%, so underlying growth is only mid-single digit.

name: Cirrus Logic, Inc.
reason: Net-cash audio/mixed-signal chip designer with 15% avg ROIC but a single dominant customer (Apple, roughly 85-90% of revenue) and design-win risk on every iPhone cycle; EPS at 1.0x its 10y high with margin at the 82nd pctile.
